claims.claim: B lent A a record the other day
claims.attribute: B performed the action of lending a record to A

evidence.quote: the record you lent me the other day

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 1 directly states 'the record you lent me the other day' — a clear presupposition that B performed the act of lending a record to A.

claims.claim: B allowed A to keep the record for a long time
claims.attribute: B granted A extended possession of the record

evidence.quote: letting me keep it so long

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 3 explicitly thanks B for 'letting me keep it so long,' directly attributing the permission/allowance to B.

claims.attribute: B is the owner of the record

evidence.quote: the record you lent me the other day
letting me keep it so long

claims.adjudication_reason: B 'lent' the record (turn 1) and A asks B 'Would you mind my keeping it for another week?' (turn 7), both presupposing B has authority over the record, strongly implying ownership. While one could lend a borrowed item, the combination of lending and being asked permission to continue holding makes ownership the most grounded inference.

claims.claim: B is in the same class as A
claims.attribute: B shares a class membership with A

evidence.quote: Everyone in our class enjoyed it

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 5 says 'Everyone in our class enjoyed it.' The possessive 'our class' is a presupposition that both A and B belong to the same class. This is a definite possessive in a statement, not a question, making it well-grounded.
